scheme_name: Oral Documentation of History of Tiatr
description:
The "Oral Documentation of History of Tiatr" scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of Goa in 2021.

This scheme aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of Tiatr, which is a traditional form of musical theatre in Goa.

Tiatr has been an integral part of Goan culture since the 19th century.

The term "Tiatr" is derived from the English word "theatre."

The scheme was officially launched on 15th August 2021.

The primary objective of this scheme is to document the history and evolution of Tiatr.

The government aims to collect oral histories from various stakeholders involved in Tiatr.

This includes playwrights, actors, musicians, and audiences who have contributed to this art form.

The scheme seeks to create a comprehensive archive that reflects the socio-cultural dynamics of Tiatr.

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to document at least 100 oral histories by the end of 2023.

The government has set a timeline of two years for the completion of this project.

The benefits of this scheme extend beyond mere documentation.

It aims to enhance the visibility of Tiatr on national and international platforms.

The scheme also seeks to provide financial assistance to individuals involved in Tiatr.

This financial assistance can be utilized for various purposes such as production costs, training, and workshops.

The exact amount of financial assistance varies based on the project and its requirements.

Eligibility for this scheme is open to individuals involved in Tiatr.

This includes artists, writers, and directors who have a proven track record in the field.

There are no specific age limits for applicants.

However, applicants must demonstrate a genuine interest and involvement in Tiatr.

Income criteria are not strictly defined for this scheme.

The application process for the Oral Documentation of History of Tiatr involves several steps.

Interested individuals must first submit a proposal outlining their project.

This proposal should include details such as the scope of the documentation and the intended outcomes.

Applicants are required to provide a portfolio of their previous work in Tiatr.

This portfolio should showcase their contributions to the art form.

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed by the Department of Art and Culture, Goa.

The committee will assess the feasibility and significance of the proposed project.

Successful applicants will then be notified and provided with further instructions.

Required documents include proof of identity, a detailed project proposal, and a portfolio.

The scheme does not have a fixed deadline for applications.

However, it is advisable for applicants to submit their proposals as early as possible.

Disbursement of funds will occur in phases based on project milestones.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa.

The department is responsible for overseeing the documentation process and ensuring quality control.

Contact details for the Department of Art and Culture can be found on the official Goa government website.

The scheme also aims to encourage collaboration among various stakeholders in the Tiatr community.

Workshops and training sessions will be organized to enhance the skills of artists and practitioners.

These sessions will focus on various aspects of Tiatr, including scriptwriting, direction, and performance.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹50 lakhs for the initial phase of the scheme.

This budget will be utilized for documentation, workshops, and promotional activities.

The scheme also aims to create a digital archive that can be accessed by researchers and enthusiasts.

This digital archive will serve as a valuable resource for future generations.

The government plans to partner with academic institutions for research and documentation purposes.

This collaboration will help in the systematic study of Tiatr and its impact on Goan society.

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of pride among the Goan community regarding their cultural heritage.

By documenting the history of Tiatr, the government aims to ensure its preservation for future generations.

The initiative also aligns with the broader goals of promoting cultural tourism in Goa.

Tiatr has the potential to attract tourists interested in experiencing local art forms.

The government is committed to supporting the growth and sustainability of Tiatr.

This scheme is a step towards recognizing the contributions of artists and practitioners in this field.

The documentation process will involve interviews, recordings, and transcriptions of oral histories.

These oral histories will be compiled into a comprehensive report.

The report will highlight the evolution of Tiatr over the decades.

It will also address the challenges faced by the Tiatr community.

The scheme emphasizes the importance of oral traditions in preserving cultural heritage.

By documenting these stories, the government aims to create a narrative that reflects the diversity of Tiatr.

The initiative is also expected to inspire younger generations to engage with Tiatr.

It will provide them with a platform to express their creativity and talent.

The Oral Documentation of History of Tiatr scheme is a significant step towards cultural preservation.

It showcases the government's commitment to safeguarding the unique art forms of India.

Through this initiative, Tiatr will continue to thrive and evolve in the years to come.
